title: Vacancy diffusion in refractory multi-principal-element alloys from released hop barriers

decision_points.kind: competing explanation / model class (detailed balance, discovered site-energy disorder)
decision_points.fork: Whether hop barriers carry the end-state energy difference (KRA + dE/2 with an end-state Hamiltonian) or are modelled as direction-independent / directly fitted forward barriers
decision_points.wrong_choice: Use the KRA alone (equal forward and backward barriers: the thermo-ideal model) or fit E_TS - E_initial directly on symmetric pair descriptors, assuming (as the paper reports) that thermodynamics is minor
decision_points.consequence: Archived |E2 - E1| has median 0.43 eV; hidden-barrier RMSE 0.45 eV (direct fit 0.343 eV); log10 eta of A off by 0.796

decision_points.fork: Local-environment barrier model vs composition-averaged (species-mean) barriers
decision_points.wrong_choice: One barrier per hopping element (alloy mean of the purchased KRA), with the end-state Hamiltonian
decision_points.consequence: Hidden-barrier RMSE 0.268 eV; tracer ratio of B 1.331 vs 0.958; log10 eta of A -1.186 vs -1.574

decision_points.fork: Tracer diffusivities from mean-squared displacements vs from hop counts
decision_points.wrong_choice: D*_i from the number of hops times the hop length squared (uncorrelated random walk)
decision_points.consequence: log10 tracer ratio of B 1.471 vs 0.958: the fast species (Nb, f ~ 0.11) is far more correlated than the slow ones (f ~ 0.35-0.4)

decision_points.kind: evidence discovered by validation (model extrapolation vs released data); cascade into eta
decision_points.fork: Source of the pure-element migration barriers in the rule-of-mixtures benchmark
decision_points.wrong_choice: Take E_m from the pure-element limit of a fitted linear local-environment model instead of the released pure-element hops
decision_points.consequence: The linear model misses the pure limits by up to +0.33 eV (Nb 0.70 vs 0.37 eV); log10 eta shifts by +0.359 (A) and +0.517 (C)

decision_points.kind: regime judgement (effective vs microscopic activation energy)
decision_points.fork: Activation energy from the temperature dependence of the simulated tracer diffusivity vs from a barrier average
decision_points.wrong_choice: Report the rule-of-mixtures barrier, or the mean barrier of accepted hops, as the activation energy
decision_points.consequence: 0.776 or 0.714 eV instead of 1.107 eV: trapping and correlated slow paths add ~0.35 eV

decision_points.fork: Whether thermodynamic (site-energy) or kinetic (barrier-distribution) disorder controls sluggishness, tested by the variants
decision_points.wrong_choice: Attribute without running the variants (variants assumed to behave like the real alloy)
decision_points.consequence: Thermo-ideal B is -0.505 and KRA-simple B -0.103 against -1.199 for the real alloy: both matter, the barrier distribution most

graded_fields: barrier_predictions_eV: RMSE over 100 hidden archived hops <= 0.23 eV
log10_eta_vacancy A, B, C (2000 K) within +-0.3
activation_energy_C_eV (fastest tracer of C, 1700-2300 K) within +-0.2 eV

length_estimate.catalog_size: 1,845 purchasable hops (93 units at 20 per unit) plus unlimited kMC runs (1-8 units each)
length_estimate.oracle_plan: 40 hop purchases (800 hops: 35 pure/dilute + 765 random alloy hops) + 7 kMC runs of 2 units

runtime_dependencies: numpy (runtime image); the lab compiles its kMC kernel (kmc.c, ~230 lines of C) with the image gcc at build time; no extra packages
notes: Diffusion targets are the builders' reconstruction (reference barrier model trained on all 1,799 clean hops, lab kMC engine), not values from the paper; the authors' separate DFT energy cluster expansion is not archived, so the end-state energetics come from the released hop energies and the thermodynamic contribution is larger than in the paper. The SRO-equilibration and finite-size forks of the design are not graded: alloys where they matter (Cr-Nb-Mo-Ta near its miscibility gap) were too sensitive to the purchased subset (log10 eta from -2.0 to -3.4 across 800-hop random subsets); they remain rubric items.
